summary: Iteration 2 tested the Vendor Portal HR sync, branding, and ran a quick regression. Backend: the existing test_employee_portal.py passes 27/27, including test_bruteforce_429, so the iteration_1 lockout bug is now fixed. The new tests/test_vendor_sync.py passes 10/10: manual sync succeeds (0 new, 9 updated), there are no duplicates on re-sync (9 vendor employees with AE/EMP/xxxxxx/yy-yy codes), status returns the latest log with no _id, and the vendor-sync endpoints require admin. The cron endpoint returns 401 with no Bearer and with a wrong Bearer, returns 200 {accepted:true} with WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET, and returns duplicate:true for a repeated X-Webhook-Id; the background run finished as success. The real employee AE/EMP/000005/26-27 logs in with the uppercase and lowercase code + 26011985, must_change_password=true, and dept/designation/bank are correct. The payslip PDF for a TEST_ employee has ARUN ENTERPRISES, the 209H/1F/1 Ops Nagar address and a logo image (checked with pypdf). Frontend (Playwright): the login page shows the logo, name, address and footer address on desktop 1920 and mobile 390 with no horizontal overflow. The sidebar shell-logo renders on desktop and in the mobile header. Admin > Employees shows the vendor sync bar. Sync now shows 'Syncing…' and is disabled while running, then the toast 'Synced: 0 new, 9 updated, 0 attendance month(s) sent'. The 9 rows all carry the 'Vendor HR' tag and the count is unchanged, and the last-sync status updates. Opening Edit on a synced employee shows emp-form-vendor-note; the dialog was closed without saving. The real employee dashboard shows change-password-banner, and the profile shows Operations / Sr. Operation Manager / Central Bank of India (read only; no punch, request or password change on it). UI regression with TEST_UI1: punch in and punch out via selfie upload with GPS verified, leave request Pending, admin approve with comment (verified as approved via the API), payslip generate (net 10,000, row shown, PDF download). TEST data was deleted. The DB check shows 0 attendance and 0 requests for vendor employees, 0 orphan records, and must_change_password is still true on the real account. No JS page errors.

minor.issue: There is no error handling per record. If one insert or update raises (e.g. DuplicateKeyError when a vendor empCode is changed to a code already used by another local user), the whole sync is marked failed after a partial update, and push_attendance is skipped for everyone. Wrap each record in try/except and collect the errors in result.
asyncio.create_task(...) result is not referenced, so the task can be garbage-collected mid-run (a known Python pitfall). Keep the tasks in a module-level set with add_done_callback(discard).

Runs synchronously inside the request (3-10s now). push_attendance also GETs the entire vendor /attendance collection on every run. As data grows this can pass the ingress timeout of about 60s. Consider running it in the background and polling /vendor-sync/status.

Additive only. If a leave is approved, pushed, and later cancelled or rejected, the vendor days are never reverted. Employees removed from or inactive in the vendor portal are updated (active=false) but never cleaned up. Confirm this is the intended business rule.

The initial password for synced employees is DOB as DDMMYYYY, which is guessable. must_change_password only shows a banner and does not force the change. Consider forcing a password change on first login.
Working/Paid Days show as '26.0' (floats). Format them as int when the value is a whole number. company name/address are still passed unescaped to Paragraph ('&' or '<' would break the PDF).

ui_bugs.issue: data-testid login-company-card and login-company-name are each used twice (desktop left panel + mobile header). On mobile, .first resolves to the hidden one. Use distinct testids (e.g. login-company-card-mobile).

issues: The footer address text is very light grey on near-white, which is low contrast. The website URL is missing there, although the desktop left panel shows it.

The Employee ID field gets autofocus with its text selected and is editable for vendor-synced employees, so it is easy to change the primary key by accident. Consider making Employee ID read-only when source=vendor.

action_items: Optional hardening: add per-record try/except in pull_employees, keep references to the cron background tasks, and consider running the manual sync in the background.
Make Employee ID read-only in the Edit dialog for source=vendor employees.
Format whole-number working/paid days as integers in the PDF, and escape company text passed to Paragraph.
Give the duplicate login testids distinct names; improve the contrast of the login footer text.
Decide whether cancelled/rejected leaves should be reverted on the vendor side, and whether the first password change should be forced.
critical_code_review_comments: The sync design is sound: match on vendor_id OR employee_id (no duplicates confirmed), the push is limited to users with vendor_id (TEST_ users are never pushed), there is a 10-minute running lock, and the cron uses an hmac compare_digest Bearer check with run_id dedupe.
Pushing never overwrites existing vendor day codes except ''/'A' -> 'P', which is safe for the live system.
pypdf was pip-installed in the container only for the test PDF text check. It is not in requirements.txt; add it if this test should run in CI.

seed_data_creation: None left behind. The sync_logs contain one cron entry with run_id TEST_run_<tag>.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: export WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET from backend/.env; REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest backend/tests/test_vendor_sync.py -n 0 (needs pypdf). It calls the manual sync and the cron, which are safe: they pull employees and push only vendor-linked attendance, of which there is none. NEVER punch, request, change the password of, edit-save or delete AE/EMP/... users. Login UI: on mobile, use .nth(1) for login-company-card. Admin requests list defaults to the Pending filter, so an approved item disappears from view.
